text:
tanya: FYI I hit a nondeterministic stale-read during a handoff test. digging in — looks like soft-evict + snapshot loader mismatch with tombstone pruning. thread below.

olivia: can you walk through the minimal repro?

tanya: W commits -> node A marks prefix soft-evict (keeps tombstones but bumps local hint) -> snapshotter S captures state (it read before W arrived) -> node B claims and loads S -> client does read-after-write and sees state before W.

raj: so snapshot freshness isn't sufficient because demote is a stronger correctness signal. we need some monotonic coordination between demote and snapshot manifests.

maria: proposal: record a small residency_token per-prefix on demote. token is monotonic (e.g., INCR key /residency/<prefix>). snapshot manifests record token_seen. claimant validates token_seen >= current token.

sahil: if token_seen < current, claimant should not blindly trust snapshot. fallback flow: 1) try to apply replay log since snapshot (cheap if small), 2) if replay log missing or too big then escalate to full rebuild. delta-first avoids heavy rebuild storms.

tanya: important: compaction might remove the replay window. in that case token mismatch forces rebuild. add metric token_rejects and reason codes (replay_missing, replay_too_large, token_gc).

olivia: race corner: demote happening between snapshot creation and claim. claimant must do a pre-claim recheck: read token T1, attempt claim, re-read token T2; if T2 > snapshot.token_seen then abort load and take fallback. that guarantees we don't silently accept stale snapshot.

raj: GC: token keys need cleanup when prefix retired. GC rule: only delete token when manifest=DELETED and tombstone_retention_elapsed. safe to have a long TTL by default.

maria: rollout: deploy snapshotter+claimant together. compatibility: missing token_seen in old snapshots => treat as 0; if current token > 0 claimant rejects old snapshot. document migration steps.

sahil: operational safety: add a circuit breaker that limits concurrent replay tasks when token_reject_rate spikes. also add an alert when reject_rate > 0.5% sustained.

tanya: perf quick run: 2k demote cycles, token bumps ~2k, snapshot rejects 0.25%, median replay apply 2.0ms, p95 6.0ms. seems OK.

olivia: also think about making snapshotter optionally subscribe to token stream so it avoids producing snapshots older than token. that reduces rejects but couples snapshotter to eviction churn. probably optional opt-in.

maria: tests: chaos harness with delayed snapshotting, forced demotes, compaction timing permutations. property test asserting read-after-write linearizability for writes that committed before demote. add logs to surface token mismatch events.

raj: add small API: SnapshotManifest { token_seen: string } and ClaimFlow pseudocode for reviewers.

tanya: I'll write RFC sketch: key layout (/residency/<prefix>), manifest field token_seen, claim validation pseudocode, replay-first fallback flow, GC policy, metrics and alerts, rollout plan. target prototype next sprint.

maria: :+1: include runbook for debugging high token_rejects and queries to inspect token key and snapshot manifests.

sahil: agreed. thanks.
